subject: MAP: Performance evaluation & TTFT streaming benchmark for chat integration (Nimble)
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha@nimble.ai>, Chris Park <chris@nimble.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, procurement@nimble.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP kickoff + proposed perf eval plan (TTFT + streaming)

Aisha / Chris —

Thanks for the time last week. Per our mutual action plan draft I promised a compact performance evaluation plan for the chat integration so we can align on closure timing. High-level asks:

- Confirm a 4-week MAP from 2026-09-20 to 2026-10-18 with a committed pilot integration window in the first week of Oct.
- We will run a streaming TTFT and end-to-end streaming latency sweep for chat generation to validate SLOs (p50/p95/p99).

Proposed test matrix (feel free to tweak):
- Models: redwood-chat-medium-fp16, redwood-chat-large-8bit
- Sequence lengths: warmed cache 256 tokens; stress 512 tokens (prompt + response)
- Concurrency: 1, 8, 32 (to mirror your expected app concurrency patterns)
- Metrics: TTFT (time-to-first-token), streaming tail latency (time per next-token, p50/p95/p99), tokens/sec throughput, CPU/GPU utilization, memory & KV-cache hit rate
- Warm vs cold: each run includes a cold-start sample set (empty KV cache) + warm runs after natural prefix warmup

Deliverables we will attach to the MAP:
- Raw CSV of per-request latencies + token timelines
- Aggregated p50/p95/p99 tables and waterfall charts
- Notes on test harness and config (batch sizes, kernel choices, quantization profile)

Could you confirm the concurrency targets and whether we should add an additional model (e.g., a quantized v1-7b-8bit) to the matrix? If procurement wants pricing/commit numbers we'll coordinate the Dedicated capacity estimate during week 3.

Next steps: I’ll queue the Redwood bench team (Marissa) to run the tests in a mirrored region once you confirm the matrix and provide a short list of example prompts (or we can replay anonymized traffic sample).

Thanks —
Rishi
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: nimble_map_scope_v1.pdf (application/pdf)]
From: Chris Park <chris@nimble.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Aisha Khan <aisha@nimble.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, procurement@nimble.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + proposed perf eval plan (TTFT + streaming)

Rishi —

This looks good. Quick clarifications from the engineering side:

- Concurrency: our production front end typically sees bursts that require up to 24 concurrent generator sessions. Can we use concurrency [1, 12, 24] instead of 32? 24 is our 99th-percentile traffic target.
- Model: please add a quantized v1-7b-8bit variant. We want to understand the cost/latency tradeoff for that size.
- Prompt set: we'll provide a 150-example anonymized sample (mix of short welcome prompts and longer multi-turn continuations).

Procurement (cc) — we’ll need a baseline Dedicated estimate for 3-month pilot pricing and any short-term burst credits.

If those adjustments are fine, please proceed and Marissa can pick the run window.

—Chris
Engineering Lead, Nimble Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Chris Park <chris@nimble.ai>, Aisha Khan <aisha@nimble.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, procurement@nimble.ai
Date: Sun, 03 Oct 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + proposed perf eval plan (TTFT + streaming) — bench results attached

Hi all —

We executed the agreed matrix 2026-10-01 -> 2026-10-02 in a mirrored us-west region. Attached are the raw CSV and a short notes file describing harness config. Summary (all times in ms):

Test conditions:
- Prompt mix: 150 anonymized examples provided by Nimble (mix: 60% short, 40% long).
- Models tested: redwood-chat-medium-fp16, redwood-chat-large-8bit, redwood-v1-7b-8bit
- Sequence target: 256 tokens nominal, stress up to 512 tokens.
- Batch behavior: continuous batching enabled, max_batch_size=16, prefix cache allowed.
- Warm runs: we ran 300 warm requests before gathering steady-state samples.

Key TTFT results (time-to-first-token, median/p95/p99):
- redwood-chat-medium-fp16 @ concurrency=1: p50=18ms, p95=32ms, p99=58ms
- redwood-chat-medium-fp16 @ concurrency=12: p50=26ms, p95=68ms, p99=140ms
- redwood-chat-medium-fp16 @ concurrency=24: p50=42ms, p95=120ms, p99=260ms

- redwood-chat-large-8bit @ concurrency=1: p50=24ms, p95=48ms, p99=90ms
- redwood-chat-large-8bit @ concurrency=12: p50=36ms, p95=96ms, p99=210ms
- redwood-chat-large-8bit @ concurrency=24: p50=58ms, p95=170ms, p99=420ms

- redwood-v1-7b-8bit @ concurrency=1: p50=28ms, p95=62ms, p99=125ms
- redwood-v1-7b-8bit @ concurrency=12: p50=46ms, p95=140ms, p99=320ms
- redwood-v1-7b-8bit @ concurrency=24: p50=82ms, p95=260ms, p99=610ms

Streaming per-token tail latency (next-token p50/p95, sample at 256 token generation, concurrency=12):
- medium-fp16: next-token p50=3.2ms, p95=8.9ms
- large-8bit: next-token p50=4.7ms, p95=12.6ms
- v1-7b-8bit: next-token p50=5.3ms, p95=15.8ms

Throughput (tokens/sec aggregate observed at concurrency=24):
- medium-fp16: 12,800 tok/s
- large-8bit: 9,400 tok/s
- v1-7b-8bit: 6,900 tok/s

Operational notes / recommendations:
- For interactive chat with p95 TTFT target <=100ms under 24 concurrent sessions, redwood-chat-large-8bit meets the goal for typical prompts (p95=170ms) but has p99 excursions; consider enabling slightly smaller max_batch_size during peak bursts to trim batching tail.
- v1-7b-8bit gives best cost/latency ratio when throughput is prioritized, but p99 shows larger tail under head-of-line contention; prefix caching and sticky routing reduced p99 by ~30% in separate runs.
- Cold-start TTFT samples (first request after idle) averaged ~280ms for large-8bit; recommend a short keepalive or synthetic warmers if you have long idle windows.

Attachments: nimble_map_bench_results_20261003.csv (per-request timeline), nimble_map_bench_notes_20261003.md (harness & config)

Happy to walk through the CSV; I can also export a short deck if procurement needs the numbers in the SOW.

—Marissa
Performance Engineering, Redwood Inference

Aisha / Chris / Procurement —

Thanks for the speedy review and thanks Marissa for the thorough run. Summary of agreed actions and MAP timeline to close: 

1) Week of 10/05 — Redwood shares final bench CSV and we provide short readout (Marissa) for Nimble engineering; action: Marissa to present in 30m sync (scheduled 10/07).
2) Week of 10/12 — Pilot integration (3-day pilot) using redwood-chat-large-8bit in a dedicated pilot pool; Redwood to provision 2-slot Dedicated estimate and a short burst credit for the pilot.
3) Week of 10/19 — Contract signature target (end of week). Procurement to confirm a one-quarter pilot PO by 10/14 to secure capacity.

Commitments:
- Redwood: deliver pilot capacity estimate and SOW addendum by 10/08; support during pilot with 24/7 on-call during test window.
- Nimble: provide final anonymized prompt set and the go/no-go on prefix warmers by 10/09.

Do these milestones look correct? Procurement — can you confirm the PO timeline so we can lock the Dedicated slots for 10/12?

If all aligned I’ll mark these milestones in the MAP and attach the bench artifacts to the HubSpot deal.

Best —
Rishi
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
